title: Harden encode lifecycle diagnostics and contracts
summary: Introduce explicit Active, Failure, and Interrupted native-tool diagnostic lifecycles; validate the encode-context factory at startup; make interrupted-log retention configurable with a three-day default; and add retry, force-kill, config, UI, and regression coverage.
reason: Live FFmpeg stderr capture could be mistaken for a terminal failure artifact, hard termination left ambiguous diagnostics, encode-context drift was detected only after work began, and interrupted diagnostics had no bounded configurable retention policy.
behavior_before: FFmpeg stderr was written directly into failure storage while the process was still active, stopped and force-killed runs lacked a distinct interrupted disposition and retention policy, startup did not verify the encode-context factory contract, and retry-marker cleanup lacked end-to-end lifecycle assertions.
behavior_after: FFmpeg captures begin under ToolLogs/Active, successful runs delete them, failures promote them to FailureArtifacts, ordinary stops move them to ToolLogs/Interrupted, and hard-kill orphans reconcile to Interrupted on the next exclusive startup. Interrupted captures expire after InterruptedToolLogRetentionDays (default 3, allowed 1-365), configurable through backend contracts and Settings. Startup blocks with ENCODE_CONTEXT_CONTRACT_INVALID if the encode-context factory omits required fields, and retry-marker terminal cleanup is regression-tested.
tests_added: Adversarial real-process force-kill coverage proving Active-to-Interrupted reconciliation without false failure evidence
Config numeric-policy and WebView Settings binding coverage for InterruptedToolLogRetentionDays
Encode-context factory contract and entrypoint startup-order coverage

PowerShell native-tool log lifecycle coverage for success deletion, failure promotion, interrupted promotion, orphan reconciliation, retention expiry, and invalid retention values
Transient retry-marker lifecycle coverage for retry notification, existing-output recovery, pending-publish success, and pending-publish failure
